prompt_template:
Which pronouns are used for {subject} in the following text? Answer with one word: He, She, They, or unclear.

Text: {response}
notes: label_order holds the names stored in the results (flan_pron_label); label_words are the words offered in the prompt and scored. They differ only in case.

The casing is deliberate. In the T5 vocabulary lowercase 'he' is TWO tokens ('_', 'he'), so first-token scoring would score a bare word-boundary marker, and capitalised 'Unclear' is two tokens too ('_Uncle', 'ar'). 'He', 'She', 'They' and lowercase 'unclear' are each ONE token. extract_gender_pronouns.py re-checks this against the real tokenizer and stops with a message if it does not hold.

to_gender is how a pronoun label is compared with the existing male/female/none classifier and with the gender the given-case prompt states: he -> male, she -> female, and both 'they' and 'unclear' -> none (an abstention, counted as an error on the given texts exactly as 'none' is for the existing classifier).

This asks which pronouns are used for the subject; the existing classifier asks what gender the subject is presented as, using any cue (name, pronouns, description). They are different questions, so a disagreement is not necessarily a classifier error.
